title: Building a single player Among Us-type game where manipulating AI NPCs is a core part of the gameplay
author: SigniLume
selftext:
I'm building a Unity single-player social deduction game where you play as impostors trying to gaslight AI NPCs, powered entirely by Gemma 3 4B (Q4\_K\_M) inference running entirely offline on the player’s device. The LLM is handling dynamically generated dialogue on the fly based on witnessed events and memory, parsing player commands, and evaluating typed defenses or accusations in court!

Started building this around when AntiGravity dropped, and used that and experimented with other AI tools over time. Currently mostly using Codex 5.3 xhigh as my main driver for coding, Opus 4.6 and Gemini 3.1 Pro for second opinions, reviews, and planning.

https://reddit.com/link/1rgpjhn/video/usffwtum25mg1/player

Using llama.cpp and LLMUnity as my runtime layer, all locally offline on the player's machine. I figured Gemma 3 4B was the best balance of decent text generation (with multilingual support!), and small enough to run on most PC gamer consumer hardware. Would love to hear how others are experimenting with AI-first gameplay!

If you're interested in checking it out, I just released the Steam store page here: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4427250/False\_Flame/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4427250/False_Flame/)

comments.author: srvs1
comments.body: What kind of machine do you need to run this model locally? Did you try more powerful cloud models?

replies.author: SigniLume
replies.body:
Running a 5070 RTX graphics card for  my own dev and play testing, but that’s probably overkill for Gemma 3 4B. I estimate a 8GB VRAM graphics card might be just enough to run the local LLM model + game + a little buffer, so something like a RTX 3060Ti could be sufficient.

I’m not trying cloud models, because that either leads to limiting requests for players eventually, or charging them for it, or having them figure out how to set up their own API keys. Local models allow the player to just download the game once then run the inference on their own machine. Downside, of course, is the quality compared to cloud models, or just larger models in general.
